## Overview

In this exercise, you will query a public REST API using R's `httr2` package, parse the JSON response, and perform basic analysis on the retrieved data.

## Task 1: Query the Open Meteo Weather API

Use the Open Meteo API (no authentication required) to fetch weather data for Fayetteville, NC:

```{r}
library(httr2)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

# Build the request
resp <- request("https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast") |>
  req_url_query(
    latitude = 35.05,
    longitude = -78.88,
    daily = "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum",
    timezone = "America/New_York",
    forecast_days = 7
  ) |>
  req_perform()

# Check status
cat("Status:", resp_status(resp), "\n")

# Parse JSON
weather <- resp |> resp_body_json()
str(weather, max.level = 2)
```

**Your turn:** What fields are in the response? Is the structure flat or nested?

> *[Your answer]*

## Task 2: Convert to a Tibble

```{r}
# Extract the daily data into a tibble
daily <- tibble(
  date = as.Date(unlist(weather$daily$time)),
  temp_max = unlist(weather$daily$temperature_2m_max),
  temp_min = unlist(weather$daily$temperature_2m_min),
  precip = unlist(weather$daily$precipitation_sum)
)

print(daily)
```

**Your turn:** What is the forecasted high temperature for tomorrow? What day has the most precipitation?

> *[Your answer]*

## Task 4: Error Handling

Deliberately cause an error (wrong URL, bad parameter) and handle it gracefully:

```{r}
library(httr2)

# Try a request that will fail
resp <- request("https://api.github.com/users/THIS_USER_DOES_NOT_EXIST_12345") |>
  req_error(is_error = function(resp) FALSE) |>  # Don't stop on error
  req_perform()

status <- resp_status(resp)
cat("Status code:", status, "\n")

if (status == 200) {
  cat("Success!\n")
} else if (status == 404) {
  cat("Not found — check the endpoint\n")
} else {
  cat("Unexpected error:", status, "\n")
}
```
